title: FedDG: Federated Domain Generalization on Medical Image Segmentation via Episodic Learning in Continuous Frequency Space
layout_note: Two panels split by a vertical dashed line: (a) the problem setting as a hub-and-spoke (client models below, server cloud in the middle, unseen target domains above); (b) what one client does locally, with its data and amplitude-spectrum thumbnails from every client.
grouping: In (a) the K clients are separated by vertical dashed lines; each is a model glyph over a dashed-outline ellipse in the client's own pastel colour (blue, yellow, green) with a padlock. A glyph legend sits in the top-left corner (source domain, unseen domain, data privacy, central server, model). In (b) the local client is a dashed rounded container titled in bold italic; the other clients' images sit below it, each tagged with its coloured domain ellipse.
shapes_depth: Flat icons: models are bow-tie (encoder-decoder) glyphs with a math label, the server a cloud outline holding a grey bow-tie, target domains filled ellipses with red dashed outline. Data are fundus photo thumbnails; amplitude spectra are small grey square thumbnails. Arrows are thin grey curves upward to the server, red curves from server to unseen domains, and curved arrows in each client's colour from its spectrum to a transformed image. Italic math labels (S^k, T^1, theta^k).
proposed_highlight: The open question is marked by red question marks and red arrows to the unseen domains; privacy is shown by a padlock on every client's data ellipse; each client's colour is carried from its ellipse to its spectrum arrow and to the image it produces in panel (b).
lesson: Give each client one pastel colour carried through its domain ellipse, its arrow and the data it contributes, and put a padlock on every data glyph so privacy is a symbol, not a sentence.
notes: Venue from the arXiv comment (Accepted to CVPR 2021). Figure type is teaser: Figure 1, problem setting plus the core idea; the full method is Figure 2.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: federated domain generalization for medical image segmentation
taxonomy.note: training other = episodic meta-learning on data transformed with other clients' amplitude spectra (continuous frequency-space interpolation)

core.what: K client columns separated by vertical dashed lines along the bottom of panel (a), each a locked source-domain ellipse under its own model glyph, all sending grey arrows up to one server cloud, which sends red arrows to unseen target domains marked with red question marks

relations.form: equal client columns S^1, S^2, ..., S^K side by side with dashed separators and an ellipsis, each holding a coloured ellipse with a padlock and a bow-tie model theta^k
grey curved arrows converge from every client model onto one bow-tie theta inside a cloud in the middle of panel (a)
the server's red arrows fan up to two dashed ellipses T^1 and T^2 plus an ellipsis, each topped by a red question mark, separating unseen target domains from the sources below
in panel (b) a small grey amplitude-spectrum tile above each other client's fundus image is passed up by an arrow in that client's colour into the local client k's dashed container

inside the 'Local client k' container a real fundus photo leads by a hollow arrow to three transformed fundus photos, one per incoming spectrum, under the title 'Transformed data with multi-source distributions'

channels.colour: client identity: each source has a pastel (blue S^1, yellow S^2, green S^K, pink S^k) carried from its ellipse to its spectrum arrow in (b); red = unknown/unseen (question marks, arrows to targets); but the target ellipses are filled orange and light blue, close to client pastels, so the unseen/seen distinction rests on the dashed red outline
channels.shape: dashed ellipse = domain, bow-tie = model, cloud = central server, padlock = data privacy, real fundus photo = data, grey square = amplitude spectrum; keyed in a legend at top left
channels.line: grey arrows = model upload, red arrows = deployment to unseen domains, client-coloured arrows = spectrum sharing; a vertical dashed rule separates the panels
channels.frame: a dashed rounded container = one client's local learning

quality.strengths: Shape glyphs are keyed once in a legend and reused in both panels; the federated star topology is drawn as geometry (client columns under one server); data are real fundus photos, and the spectrum exchange is shown by client-coloured arrows feeding transformed images, so which source contributed which style is traceable.
quality.weaknesses: The target ellipses reuse pastel fills close to the client colours, so colour alone does not separate seen from unseen; the method (episodic learning with the transformed data) is only a title in panel (b) with no learning objective drawn; panel (a), mostly the problem setting, takes as much area as the method panel.

insights.structure: Two panels split by a vertical dashed line: (a) a hub-and-spoke with K client models in dashed-separated columns at the bottom, a server cloud in the middle and unseen target domains at the top; (b) one dashed rounded container 'Local client k' above the other clients' images.
insights.data: Clients are hourglass model glyphs over dashed pastel domain ellipses (S^1 blue, S^2 yellow, S^K green) with padlocks; in (b) real fundus photographs show local data and its transformed versions, and tiny grey amplitude-spectrum squares stand for frequency-space information.
insights.emphasis: The open problem is the two unseen domains T^1, T^2 marked by red question marks and red arrows; each client's pastel colour is carried from its ellipse to its spectrum arrow and the transformed image it produces in (b).
insights.flow: (a) reads bottom-to-top, client models up into the server cloud and red arrows out to unseen domains; (b) reads left-to-right local image -> transformed images, with coloured arrows rising from other clients' spectra into the container.
insights.avoid: The corner legend is cramped and misspelled ('Data parivacy'), the padlocks and spectrum thumbnails are tiny, and (a) and (b) are tied together by nothing but adjacency.

arrangement.units: two panels side by side separated by a vertical dashed line, labelled (a)/(b) beneath; (b) has an inner dashed rounded container for the local client
arrangement.inputs_as: pastel dashed domain ellipses with padlocks in (a); real fundus photographs in (b)
arrangement.shared: amplitude spectra from every client feed the local client in (b)
